summary: You take three area courses (one each in humanities, history and social sciences) and three more East Asia content courses (one numbered 100 or above), for at least 20 units. A subplan adds language proficiency (second year, or third year for East Asian Languages) and two area courses; its additional content courses are the same ones the minor asks for. Courses outside the language requirement must be letter graded and at least 3 units. You check by hand the content and subplan area courses, which must be taught by EALC core or affiliated faculty, the 2.0 GPA, and in the East Asian Languages subplan the three language-oriented courses the DUS approves when proficiency is shown by exam. The Bulletin does not say whether a subplan's two area courses may be among the three core area courses; here they are counted as two more courses.

E0iEDEbl.why: "Complete three additional content courses offered by the EALC Department core and/or courtesy/affiliated faculty in the literature, culture, linguistics, anthropology, archaeology, art and art history, history, philosophy, political science, religious studies, sociology, or another field as approved by the DUS, SSO, or advisor of East Asia, at least one of which must be a numbered at or above the 100-level." Who teaches a course (EALC core or affiliated faculty) is not in the catalog, so the student moves the approved courses in; the 100-level course is part of that check.
